learning_outcomes.text: Demonstrate the ability to analyze and synthesize.
Acquire the ability to effectively solve problems.
Acquire skills related to the use of computer programs for calculation, data analysis, and processing within their field of application.
Develop the ability to transmit information, ideas, problems, and solutions to both specialized and non-specialized audiences.
Information search and management skills.
Possess the ability to make decisions.
Develop critical reasoning.
Develop interpersonal skills.
Develop teamwork capacity.
Ability to apply knowledge to practice.
Acquire the ability for autonomous learning and concern for knowledge and continuous training.
Develop the ability to adapt to new situations.
Ability to generate new ideas (creatvity).
Ability to work autonomously.
Motivation for quality and continuous improvement.
Achievement motivation.
Become aware of issues related to the environment.
Spatial vision capability and knowledge of graphic representation techniques, both by traditional methods of metric geometry and descriptive geometry, and by computer-aided design applications.
Knowledge and abilities to apply graphic engineering techniques.

Ability to draft and develop projects in the field of mechanical engineering for the construction, reform, repair, conservation, demolition, manufacturing, installation, assembly or exploitation of: structures, mechanical equipment, energy installations, electrical installations, industrial installations and plants, and manufacturing processes.
Ability to perform measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert reports, studies, work plans and other similar tasks.
Ability to manage specifications, regulations, and mandatory standards.
Ability to interpret projects and technical reports.
Interpret any normal object in Dihedral Projections and perspectives, and acquire sufficient reading capacity, i.e., restoring to space what is provided through projections.
Achieve elementary dexterity in drafting, especially in sketching.
Acquire knowledge of Standardization and conventions used in Technical Drawing.
Acquire sufficient knowledge of Geometry to graphically solve problems of spatial geometry applied to engineering, which may arise in professional practice.
Achieve elementary dexterity in Drafting, Sketching, and Computer-aided design.
Know how to graphically solve problems of spatial geometry applied to engineering that may arise in professional practice.
Know how to work alone and in a team, distinguishing these work times.

Know how to locate problem data information, correctly transfer it to reality, and solve problems objectively and effectively, supported by searching and collecting information from different sources.
Be able to function in the industrial world, using its graphical language.

syllabus_topics: Projection systems, fundamentals, plane figures and surfaces
Standardized representation: views, cuts, sections, breaks, dimensioning, basic elements and diagrams
Basic concepts of Joints, Assemblies and Disassemblies
teaching_methods: Completion of assignments, reports, and memoirs
Manual drafting exercises on drawing board
Basic introduction to 3D object creation using appropriate software
Group project development using CAD tools

assessment_methods.method: Theoretical Evaluation and Practical Evaluation of Projection Systems

assessment_rules: A minimum grade of 3 points is required in each evaluation to be able to average them. For the 2nd call, the recovery procedure for the Continuous Evaluation part (Board Practices, Computer Practices, Assignment) will be agreed upon with the faculty, retaining the same percentage as in the Ordinary Evaluation. The rest of the evaluation system remains exactly the same as in the Ordinary Evaluation. For exchange students, the evaluation system may be modified if the academic calendars of the home and host universities do not coincide. Students requiring exceptional evaluation due to exceptional circumstances must submit a written request to the Dean.
